description: Financial instruments and valuation, market data charts, and the calendar machinery underlying them: date objects, ranges, business-day calculations, day counts and date arithmetic.

tools.name: TimeValue
tools.description: Computes the value of a cash flow, annuity or security at a specified time given an interest rate. It handles present value, future value and arbitrary valuation dates uniformly. Use it as the core discounting function for financial calculations.
tools.usage:
TimeValue[c, i, t]
TimeValue[Cashflow[list], rate, t]
tools.notes: The rate can be given as EffectiveInterest with a compounding convention.

tools.name: Cashflow
tools.description: Represents a stream of cash payments occurring at specified times or intervals. It is the basic input to TimeValue and other valuation functions. Payment amounts and dates can both be explicit.

tools.name: Annuity
tools.description: Represents a series of equal payments made at regular intervals over a term. Variants handle payments at period end or start and growing payments. Use it with TimeValue for loan, lease and pension calculations.
tools.usage:
Annuity[p, t]
Annuity[p, t, q]
AnnuityDue[p, t]
tools.notes: AnnuityDue pays at the beginning of each period rather than the end.

tools.name: EffectiveInterest
tools.description: Represents an interest rate with a specified compounding convention, or computes the effective annual rate from a nominal rate. Conventions include periodic compounding and continuous compounding. Use it wherever a rate must carry its compounding meaning.

tools.name: FinancialBond
tools.description: Computes prices, yields and sensitivities of fixed-income securities from a specification of coupon, maturity, face value and settlement. Properties such as "Price", "YieldToMaturity", "Duration" and "Convexity" are requested by name. Use it for bond valuation and risk measures.

tools.name: FinancialDerivative
tools.description: Values options and other derivatives under specified market assumptions, supporting European, American, Asian, barrier and lookback instruments. Greeks such as delta, gamma and vega are available as properties. Use it for option pricing and hedging analysis.
tools.usage:
FinancialDerivative[instrument, params, ambient]
FinancialDerivative[inst, params, ambient, "Greeks"]
tools.notes: Add "Delta" or "Greeks" as a fourth argument to obtain sensitivities instead of the value.

tools.name: FinancialIndicator
tools.description: Computes standard technical indicators from financial time series, such as moving averages, RSI, MACD and Bollinger bands. Indicators can be applied to raw data or to FinancialData series. Use it for technical analysis and charting overlays.

tools.name: TradingChart
tools.description: Draws a full trading chart for a financial instrument, combining price candles, volume and any number of technical indicators in aligned panels. Date ranges and indicator lists are given directly. It is the most complete single-call financial chart.

tools.name: CandlestickChart
tools.description: Draws candlestick bars from open, high, low and close data, the standard way to show price action over intervals. Colors distinguish rising and falling periods. Use it for financial series where intraperiod range matters.
tools.notes: KagiChart, RenkoChart, PointFigureChart and LineBreakChart provide alternative price-action chart styles.

tools.name: KagiChart
tools.description: Draws a Kagi chart in which line direction and thickness change according to price reversals of a threshold size, ignoring time. It filters out minor fluctuations to show trend changes. Use it for reversal-based technical analysis.

tools.name: RenkoChart
tools.description: Draws a Renko chart built from fixed-size price bricks, adding a brick only when price moves by the box size. Time is not represented on the horizontal axis. Use it to see trends without noise.

tools.name: PointFigureChart
tools.description: Draws a point-and-figure chart using columns of X and O marks to record price advances and declines beyond a box size. It emphasizes support and resistance levels. Use it as a classical noise-filtering technical chart.

tools.name: InteractiveTradingChart
tools.description: Produces a trading chart with interactive controls for zooming, panning and toggling indicators. It is meant for exploration rather than static publication. Use it when investigating a price history inside a notebook.

tools.name: CurrencyConvert
tools.description: Converts a monetary Quantity from one currency to another at current or historical exchange rates. It works with Quantity objects so units stay explicit. Use it to normalize multi-currency financial data.

tools.name: DateBounds
tools.description: Gives the start and end dates spanned by a list of dates, a time series or a date granularity. It is useful for determining the extent of a dataset. Granularity specifications return the containing period.

tools.name: BusinessDayQ
tools.description: Tests whether a date is a business day in a given calendar, accounting for weekends and holidays. Calendars for many countries and financial centres are built in. Use it for settlement and scheduling logic.

tools.name: DayCount
tools.description: Counts the number of days between two dates according to a specified day-count convention such as Actual/360 or 30/360. These conventions matter for interest accrual in fixed income. Use it for precise coupon and accrual calculations.
tools.notes: DayCountConvention lists the supported conventions used by bond functions.

tools.name: DayMatchQ
tools.description: Tests whether a date matches a specified day pattern, such as a particular weekday or a business day in a calendar. It composes well with Select over date lists. Use it for recurring-schedule logic.

tools.name: DayRange
tools.description: Generates the list of days between two dates that match a specified day type, such as business days or Mondays. It combines DateRange and DayMatchQ in one call. Use it to build trading calendars and recurring schedules.

tools.name: DayPlus
tools.description: Adds a number of days of a specified type, such as business days or Fridays, to a date. It skips days that do not match the specification. Use it for settlement dates and working-day offsets.

tools.name: DateInterval
tools.description: Represents a span between two dates as a single object, useful for events with duration. It participates in overlap tests and plotting on timelines. Use it for bookings, projects and period-based data.

tools.name: DateHistogram
tools.description: Bins dated events by calendar period and draws the counts as a histogram with a date axis. Bin granularity can be days, weeks, months or years. Use it to show event frequency over time.
